title: Bounded-below enhanced etale derived descent on an open basis
statement:
Let $B$ be an arbitrary scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subschemes forming a basis: every point of every open $W\subseteq B$ lies in some $U\in\mathcal B$ with $U\subseteq W$. All categories and indexing sets are small in a sufficiently large fixed universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For an open $W$, write $\mathbf D(W_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ for the enhanced localization of complexes of constant-$\Lambda$ module sheaves at quasi-isomorphisms: it retains derived mapping complexes, composition homotopies and their higher compatibilities. Its ordinary homotopy category is $D(W_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; write $\mathbf D^+$ for its full subcategory of objects with cohomology sheaves zero below some integer. Restriction is exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

A coherent cartesian basis system is a family $M_U\in\mathbf D(U_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ with equivalences $M_U|_V\simeq M_V$ for every inclusion $V\subseteq U$ of basis members, together with composition homotopies for every string of inclusions and all higher compatibilities. Morphisms and mapping complexes are those of the homotopy limit of this restriction diagram, including their matching homotopies. Let $\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda)$ be its full subcategory consisting of systems for which a single integer $a$ satisfies $\mathcal H^i(M_U)=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and $i<a$.

Restriction gives an equivalence of enhanced categories
$$\mathbf D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\simeq\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda).$$
It identifies the full subcategories with the prescribed lower bound $a$, for every integer $a$. These equivalences commute coherently with restriction to an arbitrary open $W\subseteq B$ (using the basis members contained in $W$) and with refinement of the basis. For any enhanced parameter category $P$ small in the chosen larger universe, restriction also induces an equivalence of functor categories
$$\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathbf D^+(B_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda))\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(P,\mathscr C_{\mathrm{ub}}(B,\mathcal B,\Lambda)).$$
The integer lower bound may depend on the object of $P$. This equivalence includes coherent natural transformations and their compositions, identities and homotopies; equations supplied as coherent diagrams descend to equations in the ordinary homotopy category. No faithfulness of the family of ordinary restriction functors on ordinary derived morphisms is asserted, and no quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $B$ or of overlaps is assumed.
